claims.claim: prove that a task was registered on a host from another host and ran a payload.
claims.evidence_quote: the windows task scheduler can also be abused to conduct remote execution as part of lateral movement

claims.claim:
Security **4698** (task created) with task name, XML content including `Command` and
  `Arguments`, and `SubjectUserName`

Security 4624 type 3 from the source just before, plus 5145 access to `\\*\IPC$` named
  pipe `atsvc` (for `at`/Impacket atexec).

Task XML file in `Windows\System32\Tasks\<name>` (author, registration date, command)
  and registry `SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Schedule\TaskCache\Tree\<name>`.

claims.evidence_quote: used scheduled tasks to execute batch scripts for lateral movement with the following command: schtasks /create /s

claims.claim:
in 4688/Sysmon 1, Prefetch SCHTASKS.EXE,
4648 explicit credentials naming target; PowerShell `Register-ScheduledTask -CimSession`.

SecurityEvent | where EventID == 4698
| extend Cmd = extract(@"<Command>(.*?)</Command>", 1, EventData)
| where Cmd has_any ("cmd.exe","powershell","\\Temp\\","rundll32")
Deleted tasks leave 4699/141 and possibly TaskCache remnants; the XML file is removed.

Legitimate software creates many tasks; focus on created-then-deleted pairs and those
  created by remote logons.

4624 type 3 from source, 4698 within seconds, 200/129 showing execution, and 4699 if
cleaned, all for the same task name.

coverage: I chose every concrete claim in the skill - all Security and TaskScheduler event IDs (4698, 4699, 4700/4701, 4702, 106, 140, 141, 200/201, 129), 4624 type 3, the 5145 atsvc IPC$ pipe, the task XML and TaskCache paths, the Audit Other Object Access Events requirement, the atexec.py random 8-char task name, redirect command and 4699-after-4698 deletion, the schtasks.exe /create /s command, 4688/Sysmon 1, Prefetch SCHTASKS.EXE, 4648, Register-ScheduledTask -CimSession, the KQL hunt query and the verify chain - then fetched both listed sources and searched each page for every claim.
suggested_edits: Nothing is contradicted, but the two listed sources cover almost none of the skill: the JPCERT URL is the Tool Analysis Result Sheet index (a tool list, no artefact detail) and MITRE T1053/005 is the technique page with no Windows event IDs, so every event-ID, path and atexec claim is unverifiable. A fix PR should bump version and cite sources that state these artefacts: the JPCERT schtasks detail page https://jpcertcc.github.io/ToolAnalysisResultSheet/details/schtasks.htm (fetched 200 today; documents the TaskScheduler 106/200/201 events, the Sysmon process-create command line with schtasks /create /s, Prefetch and TaskCache), Microsoft Learn security-auditing pages for events 4698/4699/4700/4701/4702 and the Audit Other Object Access Events subcategory, a TaskScheduler event reference for 129/140/141, an Impacket atexec.py source reference for the random 8-char task name, the cmd.exe /C redirect and task deletion, and 4624/5145/atsvc documentation; MITRE T1053/005 confirms only the schtasks /create /s lateral-movement command form and atexec.py usage by menuPass.
